problem: Navigation tasks (fine-grained VLN, coarse-grained VLN, ObjectNav) are treated as isolated problems with task-specific models; naively mixing their data in one agent causes conflicting objectives and performance drops, especially on coarse-grained tasks like REVERIE.
motivation: A versatile agent should follow instructions of any granularity, and unified training could exploit more data and skills. The authors find that fine-grained language understanding helps target-oriented navigation, but simple data mixing lowers SR by 2-7% on R2R/REVERIE, so an adaptive mechanism for sharing knowledge and retrieving task-specific skills is needed.
key_idea: Add a Mixture-of-Experts to the visual queries of DUET's cross-attention, routing experts by the agent's current state (mean visual observation feature concatenated with the text CLS feature) instead of by task or token.
insight: Routing on the state (vision + language) beats token-wise, task-wise, and text-only routing on REVERIE (SR 45.67 vs 40.39 without MoE and 43-45 for other routings), while adding task embeddings hurts because it biases the router. Putting MoE on visual queries in cross-attention gives the best SPL on all tasks, better than FFN MoE. VLN pretraining (ScaleVLN init) gives ~15% SR on R2R over LXMERT init, and DAgger with sequential (unmixed) batches is critical: R2R SR is 73.69 vs 62.36 with mixed batches.
method: Unified formulation: tasks are classed by instruction granularity (fine, coarse, zero-grained); ObjectNav is treated as zero-grained language-guided navigation, and Habitat-Web demonstrations are discretized onto MP3D nav graphs (58,803 trajectories, ~20 steps).
Backbone: DUET dual-scale graph transformer (local + global cross-modal encoders with a topological map), initialized from ScaleVLN weights, CLIP ViT-B/16 visual encoder.
SAME routing: router input x_r = W_m[mean(visual view features); text CLS], a linear top-k softmax gate selecting experts per step, so expert choice adapts to the current observation and instruction.
MoE placement: experts replace the visual query projection W_q in every cross-attention layer (fewer parameters than FFN-MoE).

Training: DAgger imitation with sequential dataset sampling (ScaleVLN, R2R, RxR-EN, CVDN, REVERIE, SOON, Habitat-Web at 10:1:1:1:1:1:2, no mixing inside a batch), loss L_DAG + 0.8 * L_balance (Switch-style load balancing).
Continuous transfer: the same checkpoint is used zero-shot in Habitat via a waypoint predictor for R2R-CE and MP3D ObjectNav.

setting.backbone: DUET-based graph transformer with SAME MoE, ScaleVLN init, CLIP ViT-B/16 (fine-tuned)
setting.training_data: ScaleVLN synthetic (4.9M) + R2R, RxR-EN, CVDN, REVERIE, SOON, and discretized Habitat-Web ObjectNav human demos (58.8k trajectories); ratio 10:1:1:1:1:1:2
setting.observation: panoramic RGB (36 views) on a topological map
setting.action_space: discrete nav-graph viewpoints (waypoint predictor for continuous transfer)
setting.privileged: none at test time beyond the standard discrete navigation graph; training uses simulator DAgger supervision

results: One unified SAME model reaches R2R val-unseen SR 76/SPL 66, REVERIE test SR 48.6/SPL 37.1, CVDN test GP 7.07, and beats the multi-task ScaleVLN† baseline on all tasks (~3% SR average) and NaviLLM on R2R and REVERIE. It matches single-task SOTA (e.g. VER, GOAT) in SPL on R2R and REVERIE but trails specialists on REVERIE SR and on R2R-CE zero-shot (47 SR vs BEVBert 59), while zero-shot MP3D ObjectNav (SR 43) beats Habitat-Web (35).
limitations: Trained and evaluated mainly in the discrete graph environment; continuous-environment results are zero-shot only and clearly below specialists on R2R-CE (SR 47 vs 59).
Still trails task-specific models on some benchmarks (e.g. REVERIE SR vs ScaleVLN 57.0, SOON val vs AutoVLN); the main ablations are single-run and based on R2R, REVERIE, and ObjectNav only.
Requires a discretized ObjectNav conversion of Habitat-Web and a waypoint predictor to reach continuous settings.
